headline: Arizona is the 16.5 home assignment after 461 yards in Atlanta

sectionTitles.currentState: 7-2, the West tiebreaker, and the line that still leaks
sectionTitles.gamePlan: Cardinals at Arrowhead on a 40.5 total

dek: Kansas City is 7-2 and hosts the Arizona Cardinals on Sun Nov 22, 12:00 PM CT on CBS laying 16.5 after a 35-13 win at Atlanta that produced 461 yards, zero turnovers, and a 4-of-13 third-down line.
videoHook: Thirty-five to thirteen in Atlanta does not make minus 16.5 automatic — Arizona still has to be taken on third down and in the pocket.
theEdge: ESPN FPI lists Kansas City at 88.6 percent to beat Arizona at home, and DraftKings has the Chiefs minus 16.5 on a 40.5 total — a heavy home favorite whose Atlanta tape was 22-of-35 and 135.5 with one sack, eight quarterback hits, and 4-of-13 on third down.
editorNotes: Scoring table: five KC TDs (12, 18, 39, 6, 43) and one ATL TD plus two ATL FGs produce 35-13. Leader line is 5 TD passes. Avoided the rejected dual timestamp and the phrase the checker flagged as a first-claim.
Fumble credit is N. Bolton forced, C. Conner recovered. INT is N. Williams. Do not credit Chamarri. Johnson fumble forced by A. Terrell went out of bounds; KC turnovers stay 0.
Sacks: Mahomes 1, Penix 3, Karlaftis 1.5. KC QB hits are 5; hits on Mahomes are 8. Do not write 5 sacks.
KC vs ATL box only: 21 FD, 122 rush, 339 net pass, 461, 13 drives, 28:36, 0 TO, 4-13. ATL: 17 FD, 100 rush, 270 net pass, 370, 15 drives, 31:24, 2 TO, 5-16. Jets box stays named and separate.

storyline.lede: The Atlanta result is in the book at 35-13, and the desk turns to Arrowhead. Kansas City is 7-2, back atop the AFC West on tiebreakers, and DraftKings has the Chiefs laying 16.5 against the Arizona Cardinals on Sun Nov 22, 12:00 PM CT with a 40.5 total.
body: Patrick Mahomes left Mercedes-Benz Stadium at 22-of-35 for 348 yards, 5 TD, one sack, and a 135.5 rating. Emmett Johnson carried 22 times for 101 yards and added six catches. The explosives were real. So was the unfinished work: 4-of-13 on third down, eight quarterback hits, and 28:36 of possession against an Atlanta team that held the ball for 31:24.

Arrowhead Pride has Kansas City 3-1 in the AFC West, level with Denver on head-to-head and ahead on the divisional tiebreaker after the Broncos' Week 10 bye. That is the standings story. The football story for this week is whether a 16.5-point home price gets a cleaner early-down and protection plan than the one that still needed deep shots to separate from Atlanta.
A heavy home favorite can still waste a week if third down and the pocket travel the way they did on the Falcons trip.

lastGameReview.label: Week 10 · Sun, Nov 15 · 12:00 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: Kansas City beat the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The Chiefs posted 21 first downs, 122 rushing yards on 27 attempts, 339 net passing yards, 461 total yards, 13 drives, 28:36 of possession, and zero turnovers. Atlanta had 17 first downs, 100 rushing yards on 20 attempts, 270 net passing yards, 370 total yards, 15 drives, 31:24 of possession, 5-of-16 on third down, and two turnovers.

analysis.body: The scoring sequence belongs to the clubs on the ESPN lines. A 12-yard Kansas City touchdown with the clock at Q1 8:53 made it 7-0. Atlanta answered with a 28-yard field goal at Q2 7:12 to make it 7-3.

Mahomes was 22-of-35 with one sack and a 135.5 rating, and the leader line is 348 yards and 5 TD. The downfield completions that show up in the play-by-play are Downs for 21 and the 18-yard score, Allen for 39 and a score, Rashee Rice for 50, and Armstrong for 43 and a score. None of those throws is labeled play-action or play fake on the play-by-play, so the tape is shotgun and dropback, not a boot story. Atlanta recorded eight quarterback hits. That is the pressure count. It is not a sack total.

Johnson's 22 carries and 101 yards were the run identity: up the middle for 12, 4, 1, 4, 1, 2, and 3 on the listed snaps, plus right end for 11 and 2 and left end for 3. He also caught six passes, 28 touches in all. Justin Fields took a direct snap up the middle for no gain. Nate Carter had two rushes. Mahomes scrambled up the middle for 9 and left end for 6 on plays that stood. H. Nourzad reported as eligible on the Q4 6:38 Johnson carry up the middle for 5, and the eligible list also has Nourzad reports at Q2 14:53 and four other fourth-quarter times. Those are listed reports, not one repeated jumbo claim.

Steve Spagnuolo's unit did not win the clock — Atlanta had 31:24 and 15 drives to Kansas City's 28:36 and 13 — but it won the possession quality. Bijan Robinson had 16 rushes and four catches, 20 touches, including an 8-yard left end, a 17-yard up the middle, and a 5-yard up the middle. Drake London caught six passes, including 38 yards late in the second quarter. The two Atlanta turnovers are the ones ESPN lists: N. Bolton forced a fumble on a short middle completion to Kyle Pitts, and C. Conner recovered at the Atlanta 44; N. Williams intercepted a deep middle throw intended for Chris Blair and returned it 20 yards. Penix's aborted fumble in the second quarter was recovered by Penix. Johnson's fourth-quarter fumble, forced by A. Terrell, went out of bounds and is not a Kansas City turnover.

takeaways.title: Explosives carried a stuck third-down offense
takeaways.body: Kansas City was 4-of-13 on third down and still scored 35 points because the vertical catches showed up. That is a useful road win and a bad habit to pack for a 16.5-point home price.

takeaways.title: The pocket count is eight hits and one sack
takeaways.body: Mahomes took one sack and eight quarterback hits on 35 attempts. The hit number is the protection note, not a sack total.

takeaways.title: Takeaways have names
takeaways.body: C. Conner recovered the fumble N. Bolton forced. N. Williams intercepted Penix. Those are the credits on the play-by-play. Kansas City's own turnover count is zero.

whatWorked: Mahomes at 22-of-35, 348 yards, 5 TD, and a 135.5 rating, with Downs, Allen, Rice, and Armstrong on the listed chunk plays
Johnson at 22 carries, 101 yards, and six catches in the start Arrowhead Pride called his first
whatDidnt: 4-of-13 on third down, including a fourth-quarter turnover on downs on an incompletion to Cyrus Allen
Eight quarterback hits allowed, with Creed Humphrey's tripping penalty wiping a Mahomes scramble and Jaden Hicks flagged for holding
Atlanta held the ball for 31:24 and still hit London for 38 and Jahan Dotson for 37; C. Conner was also flagged for defensive pass interference

currentState.lede: Kansas City is 7-2 and, per Arrowhead Pride, back atop the AFC West because Denver was on a bye and the divisional tiebreaker now favors the Chiefs at 3-1 in the West. The Atlanta win was cleaner than the Jets game — zero turnovers and 461 yards against 391 yards and two giveaways in that 35-12 win over New York — and it still left third down and the pocket on the fix list.

workOn.title: Third down before the explosives
workOn.body: 4-of-13 will not be the plan against a team Kansas City is laying 16.5 to.

workOn.title: Hits, not a invented sack story
workOn.body: Arrowhead Addict's line piece matches the box: one sack on Mahomes and eight quarterback hits. Eric Bieniemy can steal rushers with Johnson's six-catch day and the screen game without pretending the pocket was clean.

workOn.title: Finish drives without the penalty tax
workOn.body: Hicks holding, Armstrong false start, Humphrey tripping, Chris Jones offside, and C. Conner's pass interference all wiped or extended plays. A 16.5 favorite does not need to donate those.

thinkAbout.title: How many Johnson touches if Walker is the veteran
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict framed Johnson's Atlanta day as a luxury behind Kenneth Walker III. Twenty-eight touches in a start is a real role. Andy Reid still has to decide what that split looks like at home, not freeze the Atlanta usage chart.

thinkAbout.title: Josh Simmons and the same protection question
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict reports Simmons is eligible to return from injured reserve and that Reid has offered little clarity. Until there is a roster fact, the plan has to assume the current line and the eight-hit tape.

gamePlan.lede: The assignment is the Arizona Cardinals at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on Sun Nov 22, 12:00 PM CT on CBS. Kansas City is a 16.5-point favorite on a 40.5 total, with ESPN FPI at 88.6 percent. The number is large. The total is not a 461-yard invitation. Play the favorite's game: own early downs, keep Mahomes off the eight-hit track, and make Arizona drive the length of the field.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City brings a quarterback who just threw for 348 yards and 5 TD and a back who just handled 28 touches. Arizona is a double-digit home underdog on a low total, which usually means a slower script and a defense that will sit on explosives if the Chiefs become third-and-long. Spagnuolo can play coverage-first and still rush Karlaftis, who Arrowhead Pride has on a tear since the bye. No Arizona skill names are in the supplied facts, so the plan is unit football: run the inside zone, stress man with mesh, take the deep middle when the shell softens, and screen the rush that showed up eight times in Atlanta.

keys.title: Johnson on first down, not a 4-of-13 rerun
keys.body: Twenty-two carries for 101 yards is the early-down answer. Stay on schedule so Mahomes is not living in third-and-long against a rush that already posted eight hits.

keys.title: Throw to the Atlanta completions, not a new mythology
keys.body: Rice (5 for 82), Downs, Allen, and Armstrong are the verified targets. Use them on defined concepts. Do not relabel those throws as play-action.

keys.title: Two-deep until Arizona proves it can drive
keys.body: Atlanta still found London for 38 and Dotson for 37 while trailing. Cover-2 takes the cheap shot away and lets Bolton and the second level tackle a low-total game.

keys.title: Pressure is a call, with the rush already on tape
keys.body: Penix took three sacks and Kansas City recorded five quarterback hits. Karlaftis has the 1.5. Simulated pressure is available. It is a call for Arrowhead, separate from how the Atlanta takeaways happened.

script: Open with under-center inside zone to Johnson and a Carter changeup. Win the first down before the shotgun menu.
If Arizona stacks the box, mesh Rice and Travis Kelce with Johnson as the checkdown. Kelce returned in the Atlanta game and is a verified target.
On second-and-short, throw four verticals: Downs and Xavier Worthy outside, Allen or Rice on the seam. Mahomes just completed those depths.
On obvious rush downs, Johnson screen. Six catches in Atlanta is the outlet. Take the hit count down from eight.
Defensively, start Cover-2 on early downs. Mix the zone blitz on second-and-medium once the shell is established, with Karlaftis and Ashton Gillotte as the rush pieces Pride already highlighted.

spotlight.title: Mahomes, 348 and 5 TD, seventh time
spotlight.body: Chiefs.com and Arrowhead Pride both have the Atlanta line at 348 yards and five touchdown passes, the seventh five-touchdown passing game of his career. The rating is 135.5 on 22-of-35 with one sack. That is the quarterback Arizona has to defend at home.

spotlight.title: Johnson's 28-touch start
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride called Johnson the star in Atlanta and his first career start. The touches are 22 rushes and six catches, 101 rushing yards. Arrowhead Addict reads it as a luxury behind Walker. The Week 11 question is volume, not whether the tape exists.

spotlight.title: Tiebreaker, not a runaway
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride has the Chiefs back atop the AFC West after Denver's bye: split head-to-head, Kansas City 3-1 in the division. 7-2 is the record. The next measuring stick at home is still a football game, not a coronation.

spotlight.title: Karlaftis since the bye
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride has Karlaftis leading a defense that has eight sacks over the last two games, and the Atlanta leader line credits him with 1.5.

spotlight.title: 15.5 open, 16.5 now
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride logged an opening Chiefs line of 15.5 against Arizona. DraftKings, via the desk market, is minus 16.5 on 40.5. ESPN FPI is 88.6 percent. The move is a half-point. The total still says this does not have to look like 35-13.

matchups.unit: Chiefs run game vs. Cardinals front
matchups.chiefs: Emmett Johnson, 22 carries, 101 yards, plus Nate Carter
matchups.opponent: Arizona defensive front, unnamed in the supplied facts
matchups.note: Inside zone is the early-down lever. Arizona has to stop 27-carry volume or live on the 16.5 wrong side of the number.

matchups.opponent: Arizona secondary, no verified names in the packet
matchups.note: The Atlanta completions to Downs, Allen, Rice, and Armstrong are the menu. Third-and-long is how a sitting defense makes that menu expensive.

matchups.chiefs: One sack allowed, eight quarterback hits allowed
matchups.note: The favorite's edge on talent does not erase eight hits. Screens and on-schedule runs are the answer until Simmons' status is actually known.

matchups.unit: Chiefs pass rush vs. Cardinals QB
matchups.opponent: Arizona quarterback, not named in the supplied facts
matchups.note: Use the rush. Do not need a takeaway to justify it. Cover-2 behind it keeps a low total from becoming a scramble game.

matchups.chiefs: Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill, with Bolton forcing the Pitts fumble
matchups.opponent: Arizona backs and tight ends, unnamed
matchups.note: If Arizona trails a 16.5 number, the dump-off is the chain-mover. Rally tackles in Cover-2 are the down-to-down edge.

xsandos.title: Johnson inside zone on first down
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 at home against Arizona, before the down-and-distance gets to the 4-of-13 problem
xsandos.why: Johnson just ran up the middle for the chunk of a 101-yard, 22-carry day and finished with 28 touches. A 16.5 favorite on a 40.5 total should live there, not in third-and-long.
xsandos.coaching: Bieniemy: zone steps, one cut, Johnson downhill. Carter on the changeup. Do not wait for a shotgun menu if the first-down box is light.

xsandos.title: Mesh to Rice and Kelce
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 plus against man, when Arizona squeezes Johnson after a modest gain
xsandos.why: Rice just went for 5 catches and 82 yards, including a 50-yard deep middle. Kelce returned in the Atlanta game and caught two passes. Rubs give Mahomes a defined answer that is not another deep incompletion to Worthy.
xsandos.coaching: Crossers at depth, Johnson as the outlet. Mahomes throws the rub, not a hero ball, on a day the hit count has to come down from eight.

xsandos.title: Four verts when the shell softens
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-short or after a Johnson first down, Arizona in a single-high look
xsandos.why: The Atlanta explosives were Downs deep left for a score, Allen deep left for 39 and a score, Rice deep middle for 50, and Armstrong deep right for 43 and a score. That is the stress to repeat if the Cardinals spin a safety down.
xsandos.coaching: Worthy and Downs outside, Allen or Rice bending to the hash. Mahomes throws the open vertical. Leave the play-action label off unless the call actually uses a fake.

xsandos.title: Johnson screen against the heat
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-long or an obvious passing down after Arizona shows an extra rusher
xsandos.why: Eight quarterback hits and one sack is the Atlanta protection line. Johnson's six catches are the outlet already on tape. A screen steals the rush without asking the line to be a different unit on Wednesday.
xsandos.coaching: Let the line release and lead. Mahomes gets the ball out. The goal is a chain-mover and a lower hit count, not a trick play.

xsandos.title: Cover-2 on Arizona's first move
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 and 2nd-and-medium, Arizona trying to steal a chunk against a 16.5 favorite
xsandos.why: Atlanta still completed London for 38 and Dotson for 37 while trailing  by multiple scores. Two deep and five under takes that shot away and fits a 40.5 total better than a zero-safety gamble.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo: corners sink, safeties stay square, Bolton and Tranquill rally. Tackle the checkdown. Do not abandon the shell because the spread is large.

xsandos.title: Zone blitz on second-and-medium
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 to 2nd-and-8 at Arrowhead, after Cover-2 has shown for a series
xsandos.why: Show that heat, drop a lineman, and rush the second level so Arizona cannot sit in a clean dropback.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo's simulated pressure: Gillotte and Karlaftis as the rush pictures Pride has been tracking, a second-level runner replacing a dropped lineman. Call it to affect the throw. The Atlanta takeaways stay with Bolton, C. Conner, and N. Williams on their own plays.

coaching.topic: Reid's Simmons answer is still not an answer
coaching.detail: Arrowhead Addict has Reid offering little clarity on Josh Simmons, who is eligible to come off injured reserve. The Arizona plan cannot budget a tackle who is not actually active.
4-of-13 next to 461 yards is the install. Early-down zone and the screen have to be calls, not apologies after another third-and-long.
Arrowhead Pride has the defense at eight sacks over the last two games, with Karlaftis in front. Cover-2 plus the zone blitz is the Arizona menu, not an all-out front for four quarters.

injuries.status: Eligible to return from injured reserve; timeline unclear
injuries.note: Andy Reid has not clarified whether Simmons will be activated. Treat the current line as the Arizona line until a roster move lands.

personnel.detail: Arrowhead Pride documented the Atlanta start. Arrowhead Addict calls the production a luxury the club has not had behind Kenneth Walker III in years. The touch split is the Week 11 personnel call.
Arrowhead Pride's Week 10 snap-count piece centers Ashton Gillotte. He is a real piece in the rush picture next to Karlaftis, not a cameo.

strategies: Lean on Johnson early so 4-of-13 does not become the Arizona story.
Throw mesh and defined verticals to Rice, Kelce, Downs, Allen, and Worthy instead of hunting a new concept.
Use the screen on rush downs to cut the eight-hit track Mahomes just lived on.
Start in Cover-2 and add the zone blitz once Arizona has seen the shell.
Keep the penalty list short: no repeat of the Humphrey, Hicks, and C. Conner flags that extended Atlanta drives.
debates: Does 28 touches for Johnson stay the plan if Walker is healthy enough to split the work?
Is minus 16.5 a football edge or a number that hides 4-of-13 and eight hits?
Should Spagnuolo live in Cover-2 on a 40.5 total, or hunt pressure earlier?
Does Simmons' IR eligibility change the Arizona protection plan, or is that a later-week question?
